question: How can the divine be both non-existent and knower dwelling on Kailasa?
premises: The divine is addressed as the non-existent.
The divine is addressed as knower of all jewels.
The divine is addressed as dwelling on Mount Kailasa.
inference: The divine transcends ordinary existence while possessing omniscience and a sacred abode.
uncertainties: asate may indicate transcendence beyond being rather than mere non-existence.
plain_english: Obeisance to the non-existent, obeisance to the knower of all jewels, obeisance to the dweller on Mount Kailasa.
